definitions.explanation: A divine being or supreme deity; the polite form of {神|かみ}.
Colloquially used to describe someone with godlike skill in a particular area.

examples.japanese: {神様|かみさま}にお{祈|いの}りした。
{神様|かみさま}、どうか{助|たす}けてください。
{彼|かれ}はギターの{神様|かみさま}と{呼|よ}ばれている。
examples.english: He is called the god of guitar.

notes:
{神様|かみさま} is the polite/respectful form of {神|かみ} (god). The suffix 〜{様|さま} adds respect.

Usage:
- In Shinto context, refers to the many {神|かみ} (kami/deities)
- In monotheistic context (Christianity, etc.), refers to God
- Colloquially describes masters of their craft

Common expressions:
- {神様|かみさま}にお{祈|いの}りする (to pray to God)
- 〜の{神様|かみさま} (god of ~, master of ~)
- お{客|きゃく}{様|さま}は{神様|かみさま}です (The customer is god - customer service phrase)

Related:
- {神|かみ} (god - less formal)
- {神社|じんじゃ} (Shinto shrine)
